name: Newcastle East
tagline: The old headland between the harbour and the beach
description: The original settlement on the point, with terrace houses, the ocean baths, Fort Scratchley on the hill and Nobbys Beach at the end. It is the most walkable part of the city, with the harbour on one side and the surf on the other, and the light rail terminates here.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the beach and the harbour both within a five-minute walk
pros: Ocean baths and two beaches on the doorstep
Light rail and the whole centre walkable
Restored terraces rather than apartment blocks
cons: The highest rents in the city
Busy with visitors on summer weekends

name: Cooks Hill
tagline: Darby Street's cafes and galleries, one street back from the sand
description: The inner suburb behind Bar Beach, built around Darby Street with its cafes, bookshops and small galleries. Federation cottages on narrow streets, a strong local character and a ten-minute walk to the surf. It is the address most people mean when they say they moved to Newcastle.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting cafes at the door and the beach ten minutes away
pros: Darby Street's cafes, restaurants and galleries
Ten minutes on foot to Bar Beach
cons: Rents near the top of the local market
Small period cottages with little storage

name: Merewether
tagline: The surf suburb, with the largest ocean baths in the southern hemisphere
description: South along the coast, built around Merewether Beach and its enormous ocean baths, with a headland walk connecting it back to Bar Beach. Quieter and more residential than Cooks Hill, with a strong surfing population and a small run of cafes near the sand.
bestFor: Surfers who want the break below the window and a quiet street behind
pros: One of the best surf beaches in New South Wales
Ocean baths and the clifftop walk
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes from the city centre
Beach parking fills early in summer

name: Hamilton
tagline: Beaumont Street, where the city eats
description: An inner suburb west of the centre built around Beaumont Street, which holds the most concentrated and most affordable eating in Newcastle, with Greek, Italian, Vietnamese and Lebanese businesses that have been there for generations. Housing is workers' cottages and small blocks at rents below the coast.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting good cheap food and rents below the beachfront
pros: The best and cheapest eating in the city
Rents well below the coastal suburbs
Own train station and good bus links
cons: Twenty minutes to the nearest beach
Rail line noise on some streets

name: Lake Macquarie (20 km south)
tagline: The largest coastal saltwater lake in Australia
description: The suburbs strung around a lake more than twice the size of Sydney Harbour, twenty kilometres south of the city, with sailing, kayaking and a much quieter pace. Housing is family homes with gardens at rents well below inner Newcastle, and the train line runs along the western shore.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting space, water and a lower rent, with a car
pros: Sailing and paddling on the lake at the door
Houses with gardens at moderate rents
Train line into Newcastle and Sydney
cons: Thirty to forty minutes into the city
A car is close to essential
